title: Music stays under the words
statement: Keep music under the narration, lowest where it teaches, and check the final mix by ear for clear words, not only the clean voice track.
detail: The narrated opening's original score had passed technical level checks but had never been auditioned, and the handover states that technical audio measurements do not establish musical quality, intelligibility under speech or acceptable transitions. Its mixing rules keep speech consistently intelligible, lower the score under narration with ducking where useful, and check that the mix neither pumps distractingly nor becomes loud in pauses, so the score stays subordinate during narration. The check is made on the exported file at the start, every scene transition, the most intense musical passage and the ending, because a waveform or a codec report alone is not an audition.
against: No delivery target was agreed: "Exact mastering targets should be selected and documented for the delivery platform; they have not been agreed here." (`g9-archive/handover-2026-10-06/Othello-handover-docs-and-transcript-2026-10-06.zip!/Othello-handover/Othello-project-handover.txt`, line 323). No person has listened to the mix, at normal or quiet level (`g9-film-v01-render/QA.md`, lines 3 and 122), and whether its ducking "reads as breathing or as pumping is a listening judgement" (the same file, line 94). Transcription over music is noisy in its own right: one timing offset was "whisper's own early bias over music, not caption lateness" (the same file, line 76), and a misheard name did not reproduce on an immediate re-transcription of the same mix segment (the same file, line 114).
